newsitem.title: ITALY: Mafioso wants to study theology but bishop says no.
newsitem.headline: Mafioso wants to study theology but bishop says no.

text.p: Arrested Mafia boss Pietro Aglieri, once one of the Sicilian mob's most ruthless killers, wants to study theology but a leading Sicilian bishop said no on Thursday.
Aglieri, who was arrested earlier this month, told newspapers through his lawyer that he had a "strong desire" to sign up for a theology course through a Sicilian university.

The lawyer, Rosalba Di Gregorio, said she had told him it would be difficult for him to get permission to study from jail by correspondence course because of laws that limit contact with the outside world for arrested Mafiosi.
The bishop of the Sicilian city of Catania said Aglieri would not be allowed to study theology even if civil law permitted it.
Bishop Luigi Bommarito said Roman Catholic Church law did not permit Mafiosi to take the sacraments or study theology from a Church-approved university.
Bommarito said he questioned the motives behind the Mafioso's desire, suggesting the move was more an attempt to change his image than a sign of remorse for past crimes.
Investigators believe that before his arrest Aglieri may have taken control of Cosa Nostra after godfather Salvatore "The Beast" Riina was captured in 1993.
Aglieri was arrested in an operation involving hundreds of policemen east of the Sicilian capital Palermo.
